meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-14 | Time: 15:00 - 15:46 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Sinha (Redwood SE) — Claire Whitman (Elmwood), Dorian Lee (Elmwood), Samir Khatri (Elmwood), Priya Rao (Elmwood)
summary: Intro discovery on Elmwood's security constraints and deployment preferences. Main concerns: KMS integration, audit log retention, SAML/SSO integration, RBAC and least-privilege for model access, data residency for EU customers, and fallback SLA for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreed to send attestation docs and schedule Dedicated benchmark session.
topics: SOC 2 / ISO attestation and recent pen-test
Encryption at rest, in transit, and KMS/HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Network topology and VPC peering / private link
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking the time um we'll do a quick intro, we're from Redwood inference, I'm Maya AE and Jordan is our SE, uh Ravi's here to help on deployment specifics.
[00:14] Claire Whitman: hi thanks, Claire here, head of platform at Elmwood. We're trying to understand security posture options for running LLM features across our agent workflows.
[00:28] Jordan Patel: great; high level can you describe constraints — e.g., do you need anything on-prem, or is a VPC/private deployment sufficient?
[00:41] Dorian Lee: we have two buckets: EU customer data must stay in EU and we prefer customer-managed keys. Secondary is low-latency for some underwriting calls — <laugh> not like financial trading low but still sensitive.
[00:58] Maya Chen: makes sense. quick callout: we support hosted with region pins, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC / on-prem) — for customer-managed keys we integrate KMS via bring-your-own-key patterns and HSM for private deployments.
[01:15] Samir Khatri: can you describe how the KMS integration looks? e.g., who holds the keys, is there a pass-through, or do you encrypt at rest with our CMK?
[01:30] Jordan Patel: good question. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption where Redwood holds a wrapped key but you can rotate a CMK in your cloud KMS and we keep only encrypted blobs. for Private, the control plane is optional — in VPC mode the inference nodes can be configured to use your KMS directly so private keys never leave your account. sometimes the transcript parser eats jargon — I said 'envelope' like enve-lop.
[01:56] Dorian Lee: ok, do you support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault and GCP KMS?
[02:05] Jordan Patel: yes we have integrations for AWS KMS and Azure, GCP in beta for Private. For Dedicated we provision isolated GPU pools and you can attach KMS through customer-provided IAM role.
[02:20] Priya Rao: are you SOC 2 certified? and do you have ISO27001? we need attestation and a penetration test report.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates — I'll share the PDFs and the latest pen test summary. we also publish a security questionnaire.
[02:42] Claire Whitman: great. audit logs — we need per-request audit trails with export to our SIEM for 7 years. can you do that?
[02:53] Jordan Patel: we capture request-level metadata and have an audit stream you can forward to an S3 bucket or to a SIEM via HTTP forwarding. retention is configurable at the org level; default retention on Hosted is 90 days but for Dedicated/Private we can increase or make it customer-managed. seven years is long — typically handled by customers after export but we can supply nightly exports.
[03:20] Samir Khatri: is there a canonical schema for logs? we want stable fields for request id, model id, prompt hash, redacted PII flag, response tokens, and outcome code.
[03:33] Jordan Patel: yes we have a documented audit schema — I'll attach the doc. note the schema has fields that may evolve; for PII we recommend client-side redaction + server-side redaction hooks.
[03:47] Claire Whitman: SSO — we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning. can Redwood integrate with our IdP and enforce RBAC scoped to teams?
[03:58] Maya Chen: absolutely; we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for users and groups. RBAC is layered — org->project->model role bindings. you can configure least-privilege roles and also create API tokens scoped to routes/models.
[04:16] Dorian Lee: do tokens expire and is there session revocation?
[04:20] Jordan Patel: tokens have TTLs; API tokens can be rotated, and we emit revocation events to the audit log. session-based SAML SSO sessions will honor your IdP session settings.
[04:34] Priya Rao: encryption in transit — do you have mTLS between control plane and inference nodes?
[04:41] Jordan Patel: yes, control plane comms use mutual TLS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted uses TLS with endpoint certificates and client certs optional in Private. sometimes the auto-transcript shows 'M T L S' as letters.
[04:56] Maya Chen: another practical tradeoff is fallback: if Dedicated pool is saturated do you want automatic fallback to Hosted variants? some customers allow it, others with tight data rules disable fallback.
[05:10] Samir Khatri: we need a policy: no data ever leaves our VPC, so fallback is not allowed. how does Redwood enforce that?
[05:18] Jordan Patel: in Private/VPC mode we can disable outbound fallback and failover to hosted; we also can enforce egress rules via security groups and route tables.
[05:31] Dorian Lee: network wise we use Transit Gateway peering and strict NACLs; can Redwood's nodes live in our subnets?
[05:40] Jordan Patel: yes Private supports deploying nodes into your subnets via a CloudFormation/Terraform module — we give a module that creates roles, subnets, SGs and the inference autoscaling groups. we'll share the Terraform module.
[05:54] Claire Whitman: that'd be useful. are there compliance logs for who accessed which model and when? that is key for audits.
[06:03] Maya Chen: audit logs include user, API key, action (generate/embed), model version, timestamp, and request metadata. we also provide signed export bundles for compliance purposes.
[06:18] Samir Khatri: token-level billing / cost attribution matters — we want token-level breakdown per model to map to internal chargeback.
[06:26] Jordan Patel: console provides token-level cost breakdown; you can also stream the raw usage metrics to your billing system.
[06:35] Dorian Lee: what about running models with quantized weights for cost savings — any impact on safety or encryption?
[06:44] Jordan Patel: quantization is an execution optimization; encryption at rest applies to the model artifacts and checkpoints as files. for private we store model artifacts in your storage; for hosted/dedicated we manage artifacts but keep them encrypted and hashed.
[06:58] Claire Whitman: incident response — do you have an IR playbook and notify customers for security incidents?
[07:06] Maya Chen: yes we have incident response SLAs, we notify customers within our contractual windows and provide root cause and mitigation steps. redwood has SOC incident channels.
[07:18] Priya Rao: data retention policy — for Hosted you said 90 days default; can we opt for zero retention for sensitive endpoints?
[07:27] Jordan Patel: yes we support zero retention/no-logging mode for specific routes; note that disables some observability features like per-token cost logs and long-term evaluation.
[07:40] Samir Khatri: what about de-identification? can the service mask PII at ingestion?
[07:46] Jordan Patel: we offer a pre-processing hook — you can run a redaction lambda before sending to Redwood or use our built-in redaction rules but client-side is recommended for strong guarantees.
[07:59] Claire Whitman: curious: what are typical SLA numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:05] Maya Chen: Hosted has a higher variable latency tail but is easier to scale; Dedicated gives you SLA-backed throughput and latency SLOs — we publish p50/p90 targets per model in the catalog. for Dedicated customers we commit to an uptime SLA and a latency objective in contract.
[08:22] Dorian Lee: can we bring our own models into Dedicated or Private?
[08:28] Jordan Patel: yes, you can bring custom models — we support custom model onboarding and provide a verification runbook; for hosted we sandbox models but you can upload via secure channels.
[08:40] Claire Whitman: regarding RBAC for models, can we restrict certain model families to specific teams? e.g., only Risk team can call 'riskx-large'.
[08:49] Maya Chen: yes, role bindings can be set per-model or per-route; group-based enforcement uses SCIM groups from your IdP.
[08:59] Samir Khatri: about logs again — if we export logs to an S3 bucket, are they encrypted server-side and can we enforce SSE-KMS?
[09:08] Jordan Patel: exports to customer buckets support SSE-KMS, and you can configure bucket policies to restrict Redwood’s write-only role.
[09:18] Priya Rao: do you maintain change logs / config history so we can see who changed model permissions?
[09:25] Jordan Patel: yes we keep an immutable config audit trail and show who changed RBAC bindings; this is included in audit exports.
[09:35] Claire Whitman: any blockers for us to run a short pilot? we'd like private deployment to meet our zero-logging and CMK requirements.
[09:44] Maya Chen: sounds feasible. next step we will share the SOC/ISO artifacts, Terraform module, and schedule a Dedicated benchmark. if you want zero-logging we can provide a checklist for required config changes.
[09:58] Dorian Lee: one more: how do you handle model caching and KV cache concerns with PII — could KV cache hold sensitive tokens?
[10:08] Jordan Patel: KV cache is ephemeral and can be disabled per-route; for sensitive data we recommend disabling caching or encrypting cached entries with your KMS. we often see the phrase 'K V cache' in notes.
[10:23] Samir Khatri: perf: do you support GPU isolation per-customer to prevent noisy neighbor?
[10:29] Jordan Patel: Dedicated uses tenant-isolated GPU pools, and Private runs in your VPC so physical isolation is controlled by you. for hosted we use soft isolation and scheduling to reduce noisy neighbor effects.
[10:43] Priya Rao: audit: can we get SOC 2 controls mapping to our security framework?
[10:49] Maya Chen: yes we provide a control-mapping for SOC 2 sections to common frameworks; I'll attach that.
[11:00] Claire Whitman: ok thanks. we'll review artifacts. do you have a standardized security questionnaire?
[11:06] Maya Chen: yes, we have an infosec questionnaire; I'll populate a prefilled version and send it.
[11:12] Dorian Lee: for Private — do you support air-gapped environments? we have a legacy PIH system that is occasionally air-gapped.
[11:21] Jordan Patel: we offer an on-prem package that can be deployed air-gapped, with manual attestation steps and offline license keys. that's more involved but customers in regulated spaces use it.
[11:35] Samir Khatri: provisioning: how long to stand up Private in our VPC?
[11:40] Jordan Patel: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on networking approvals and our onboarding window. Dedicated is faster if you accept our managed infra.
[11:50] Claire Whitman: last Q: are there hard limits on model artifacts size or sequence length that affect encryption or retention?
[11:58] Jordan Patel: large artifacts are stored as blobs and encrypted; we have recommended size tiers and can discuss specifics in the benchmark meeting.
[12:10] Maya Chen: ok, timebox — recap and next steps. I'll send artifacts and the Terraform module and we will schedule the benchmark. Jordan will prepare diagram and logs schema.
[12:25] Claire Whitman: thanks everyone.
[12:29] Maya Chen: thanks all.
[46:00] Meeting ended
notes: Customer emphasized zero-logging for certain routes, CMK requirement, and long-term audit retention. Redwood to provide documentation + Terraform module + schedule benchmark. Customer will provide traffic profile for sizing.
